fixture_name: A9 Ballinluig SB signage/VRS-adjacent visibility — real UK Stage 1&2 RSA (Transport Scotland OGL release)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Constrained forward visibility from curve-plus-vegetation on an off-slip approach, with a shared driver/pedestrian verge corridor, is a genuine, location-specific hazard and the finding converts the logged remediation duty into a verified handover condition rather than restating it vacuously.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claims (visibility reduction, pedestrian-passage requirement, agreed extension action) are all directly supported by the verbatim EV-UK-025 quote, with EV-UK-002 used only as context; only the phrase 'both logged problem locations' mildly conflates two issues with two locations.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as a safety_concern with no compliance/normative basis asserted, respecting GG 119 semantics where the auditor raises problems and seeks designer action rather than enforcing compliance clauses.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (deliver and evidence extended clearance covering both issues, confirm post-clearance visibility and pedestrian passage before handover) and clearly viable, though it lacks quantitative acceptance criteria such as a required SSD or minimum verge width.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly named as affected road users, the cited log entry expressly requires clear pedestrian passage, and the scenario confirms VRUs are in scope, so vulnerable-user impacts are fully considered and central to the recommendation.
